close_reason: Added pub(crate) truncate_for_detail helper (256-byte cap, UTF-8 char-boundary-safe, Cow-borrowed on the no-truncation fast path). Wrapped all attacker-controlled interpolation sites in rfc8398 (SAN entry strings — the bead's primary concern) and the der::Error::to_string() sites in rfc5280, rfc6125, rfc8398, rfc8551. Bounded-shape interpolations (usize, ObjectIdentifier) left as-is. Five regression tests cover the helper. 307 tests pass; clippy clean.
description:
rfc5280.rs, rfc6125.rs, rfc8398.rs, rfc8551.rs use format!() to interpolate attacker-supplied byte content from parsed certificates into LintResult::error detail strings with no upper length bound. Examples:

- pkix-lint/src/rfc8398.rs:322-326 — `format!("rfc822Name SAN entry '{r}' is malformed ...")` where `r` is an arbitrary-length SAN entry string parsed from the cert
- pkix-lint/src/rfc8398.rs:331-335 — same for SmtpUTF8Mailbox entries
- pkix-lint/src/rfc8398.rs:349-353 — same in the no-matching-equivalent branch
- pkix-lint/src/rfc6125.rs:137-140 — `format!("SubjectAltName extension value is malformed DER: {e}")` where `e` is a der::Error containing possibly arbitrary bytes
- pkix-lint/src/rfc5280.rs:276-279, 393-398 — similar shape for malformed extension errors

Section C (untrusted input at protocol boundaries). What goes wrong: integrity / availability. A malicious certificate carrying a 100MB rfc822Name SAN entry causes:
1. A 100MB `LintResult::Error(Cow::Owned)` allocation per failing lint
2. That detail string travels through `Finding` → OSCAL JSON emit (`risks_from_store`, `observation_for_evidence`, `finding_for_lint_result`) — at minimum a 2× copy through serde_json
3. Downstream OSCAL consumers ingesting the audit JSON face the same amplification on parse

The cert itself is bounded by upstream DER parser limits (x509-cert), but the rfc822Name IA5String content has no length cap that x509-cert enforces — IA5String accepts arbitrary length under SIZE constraints rfc5280 does not formally tighten.

Severity P2: not a code-exec defect, but turns a single malicious cert into worst-case 100MB×N-lints×emit-copies memory pressure on any pkix-lint pipeline. Realistic CI / OSCAL importer process gets OOM-killed.

Fix shapes:
- Truncate interpolated values at a documented cap (e.g., 256 bytes) with a `(truncated)` marker, similar to how OpenSSL trims X509_NAME_oneline output
- Or move the byte content into a separate `Finding.evidence_bytes: Option<Vec<u8>>` field with explicit caller opt-in for inclusion
- Or replace value interpolation with index-only references (`SAN entry index 3 has malformed local-part`) and document that operators must consult the cert for byte content

This finding is in scope for crypto-security (Section C) even though pkix-lint does not handle secrets: certificates are attacker-influenced bytes crossing a protocol boundary, and bounded-output discipline is part of the protocol-boundary contract.
title: Unbounded attacker-controlled cert content interpolated into LintResult::error detail strings
